Preprint — arXiv:2610.22732v1 [cs.CL], 15 Oct 2026; no venue stated
UC Berkeley (Li, Yu, Stoica); Microsoft Research (Xu, Singh, Inala, Galley, Gao); Microsoft Security (Chen, Siska, Tamersoy). First author's work done during a Microsoft Research internship

Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — TokenEconomizer, external experience-driven cost controller for black-box coding agents, compared with default high effort, medium/low effort, RTK, RepoMap and combinations across 3 agents, 5 agent-model settings and 4 benchmarks; preceded by a cost-profiling study of fixed strategies

TokenEconomizer (no version; code at github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer): three meta-strategies learning repository-specific policies from completed traces: (I) experience-grounded micro-skills (one-line operational facts with regex/predicate detectors, activated after confirmation, retired on contradiction), (II) tool pruning (unused for 3 tasks or judged irrelevant; full-catalog re-audit every 5 tasks), (III) failure-loop intervention (turn budget 1.25x 90th percentile of passed turns, LLM judge redirect then stop). Baselines: reduced reasoning effort; RTK v0.45.0 (command-output compression); Aider RepoMap; Serena (profiling only)

Micro-skill manual (short list of operational facts) inserted between harness instructions and task description; loaded tool set; repository state (skills, evidence, tool history, turn statistics). No specification

Per task in a chronological stream: controller decides active micro-skills, tool set and turn budget from repository state -> agent runs task -> live guard checks for loops (redirect/abort) -> completed trace updates state; proposer drafts candidate micro-skills after task 4 and every 5 tasks
None (fully automatic controller)

Full approach run on unchanged agents (all three meta-strategies acting on the prompt prefix, tool configuration and event stream); ablations run each meta-strategy alone. Not an SDD approach; of the form's categories the closest is 'single artefact' (micro-skill manual injected into the prompt), but tool pruning and the loop guard are not artefacts

fields.why: All numbers checked against Tables 1-2 (p. 8-9). The paper reports only relative cost changes, so every cost verdict is necessarily relative to default and default's cost cannot be judged ('not judgeable' is outside works/partly/does not work); quality levels (e.g. CredData F1 about 68 'partly', SWE-Bench Pass@1 65-70 for low effort 'partly') are a judgement

fields.v: Tasks: chronological task streams per repository/project; same tasks and order for all methods and seeds; answer-key guard blocks GitHub access for all methods. Configurations: 8 methods x 5 agent-model settings on SWE-Bench; TE vs default on Web-Bench and security benchmarks (micro-skills disabled on security). Baseline: unmodified agent at high reasoning effort. Held constant: agent version, model, tasks and order, controller configuration (fixed before main runs from development runs on the same six repositories, not tuned per repository). Acceptance: official graders. Repetitions: 3 seeds. Human intervention: none

TE reduces SWE-Bench cost by 18.4-30.9% (incl. controller overhead) with Pass@1 above default in 4 of 5 settings (-1.0 pt on Opus 4.8); reduced effort saves 16.8-45.5% but loses 1.8-10.3 pts; RTK and RepoMap alone change cost inconsistently (RTK raises cost in 12/30 repository-setting cells, RepoMap in 15/30). TE lowers cost in all 30 cells (5.2-40.1%); TE+RTK in 30/30, TE+RepoMap 29/30. TE variants form every Pareto point at or above default pass rate. Cumulative savings 16.9-32.0% after initial overhead (cheaper by sixth task). Web-Bench -16.0 to -21.2%, CredData -16.5 to -19.6%, ReposVul -6.4 to -9.3%. No significance tests; SDs over 3 seeds

Distinguished methods on cost consistently across repositories and settings; Pass@1 differences of 1-2 points comparable to seed SDs. Repeatable: 3 seeds with SDs; config fixed in advance; code released. Limitations stated: controller decisions can be wrong (stale skills, needed tool pruned, productive task taken for loop), each with a recovery path; minimal harnesses not covered; SWE-Bench streams are independent fixes, not real user sessions; Codex hook not invoked in its version (guard relies on DNS block)

Coding-agent costs accumulate across tasks in recurring environments; an external controller learning from completed work makes unchanged agents cheaper while largely preserving success. Gaps: interactive coding sessions as next test; minimal harnesses; broader class of external controls (effort/model choice, learned compaction, environment reuse)
